documents.title: Board Meeting Intimation for Consideration And Approval Of The Un-Audited Financial Results For The Quarter Ended 30Th June, 2026
Compliances-Certificate under Reg. 74 (5) of SEBI (DP) Regulations, 2018

analysis.summary: For FY 2024-25, Pasupati Acrylon reported revenue from operations of Rs. 62,143.18 Lakh, up from Rs. 57,522.82 Lakh in the previous financial year. Profit after tax rose to Rs. 3,538.12 Lakh compared to Rs.

guidance.claim: The company expects to commence commercial production at its 150 KLPD grain-based ethanol project by September 2024.
guidance.quote: Further, the Company has already initiated steps to establish grain based Ethanol Project with a production capacity of 150 KLPD and it is expected to commence commercial production of Ethanol by September, 2024.

guidance.claim: The company expects sales and production to improve further in the coming years, though it remains cautious of inflation and high energy prices.
guidance.quote: The sale and production has seen good improvement from previous year and it is expected to improve more in the coming years but it is necessary to carefully watch other factors such as inflation, high energy prices etc.

demand_outlook.claim: The company expects sustained growth in demand across its business segments.
demand_outlook.quote: Your Company anticipates sustained demand growth across segments.

demand_outlook.claim: Demand for acrylic fibers is projected to grow in the coming years due to macroeconomic growth in end-use sectors.
demand_outlook.quote: The demand for acrylic fibers is anticipated to rise in the coming years, particularly due to the macroeconomic development of end-use sectors which is supported by regional GDP and population growth.

demand_outlook.claim: The market for CPP films is expected to expand due to increasing convenience food consumption and packaging demand.
demand_outlook.quote: The market for CPP Films is expected to increase in the near future due to the rise in the consumption of convenience foods and the high need for packaging solutions.

demand_outlook.claim: Revenue and net profit for FY 2023-24 declined due to lower demand for acrylic fibre and falling selling prices in the CPP segment.
demand_outlook.quote: Revenue and Net profit during the year declined due to lower demand of acrylic fibre and negative return on CPP Segment caused by persistent fall in selling prices on account of excessive production capacity added in the market.

demand_outlook.claim: CPP film sales and production improved in the final quarter of FY 2023-24 due to better market sentiments.
demand_outlook.quote: During the year, the sale and production was declined due to lower demand but in the last quarter of FY 2023-24, it was improved due to better sentiments in the market and it is expected to improve in the coming years.

demand_outlook.claim: Demand for Acrylic Fibre has increased, leading to higher production and sales compared to the previous year.
demand_outlook.quote: Demand of Acrylic Fibre has risen and the Company’s production and sales of Acrylic Fibre was 36,425 MT and 35,260 MT respectively as compared to production of 29,652 MT and sales of 30,918 MT during the previous year.

demand_outlook.claim: The company's exports grew significantly during the year to 4,551 MT.
demand_outlook.quote: During the year, the Company’s exports have grown to 4,551 MT as compared to last year’s exports 1,415 MT.

capex_expansion.claim: The company commissioned its 150 KL per day grain-based ethanol plant and started commercial production in March 2025.
capex_expansion.quote: The Company has successfully commissioned its 150 KL per day grain-based Ethanol Plant and commenced commercial production in March, 2025.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has spent approximately Rs. 188 Crore on the ethanol plant project, funded via Rs. 104 Crore of term loan and the rest from internal accruals.
capex_expansion.quote: Company has spent around Rs. 188 Crore so far which includes Rs. 104 Crore of Term Loan and Balance amount out of internal accruals.

capex_expansion.claim: A 750 KW solar power system has been installed by the company.
capex_expansion.quote: Solar Power System of 750 KW has been installed.

capex_expansion.claim: The Board of Directors approved setting up a 150 KLPD Ethanol Project on May 18, 2022.
capex_expansion.quote: Board of Directors, at its meeting held on 18th May, 2022, had accorded its approval to the Company to set-up Ethanol Project with a production capacity of 150 KLPD to align with GOI’s Ethanol Blending Programme (E20), subject to clearance and approvals from the concerned statutory authorities.

capex_expansion.claim: The total project cost for the Ethanol Project is Rs. 167.58 crores.
capex_expansion.quote: The total Project cost is Rs. 167.58 crores.

capex_expansion.claim: Indian Bank sanctioned a term loan of Rs. 108 Crores for the Ethanol Project with the remaining Rs. 59.58 Crores to be met from internal accruals.
capex_expansion.quote: Indian Bank had sanctioned Term Loan of Rs. 108 Crores and as per stipulations of sanction letter, the remaining project cost of Rs. 59.58 would be met out of the Company’s internal accruals.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has spent approximately Rs. 92.17 Crores on the Ethanol Project, including Rs. 44.08 Crores from the term loan.
capex_expansion.quote: However, the Company has already spent around Rs. 92.17 Crore so far which includes Rs. 44.08 Crores of Term Loan and balance amount out of internal accruals.

capex_expansion.claim: The company will fund Rs. 59.58 crores of the Ethanol project cost from internal accruals.
capex_expansion.quote: The remaining project cost of Rs. 59.58 will be met out of the Company’s internal accruals.

capex_expansion.claim: The company has obtained Environment Clearance for the proposed Ethanol project and is finalizing vendors.
capex_expansion.quote: The Company has obtained Environment Clearance for the proposed project and company is under process to finalize various vendors/ suppliers / consultants for the projects and releasing advances to them as per contract out of its Internal Accruals.

margins_costs.claim: CPP film loss before tax, exceptional items, and interest declined to Rs. 30.62 Lakh from Rs. 412.28 Lakh in the previous year.
margins_costs.quote: Loss before tax, exceptional items and interest was Rs. 30.62 Lakh as compared to loss of Rs. 412.28 Lakh in the previous year, reflecting an improvement of 92.57%.

margins_costs.claim: The reduction in CPP losses was driven by better realization and lower overheads.
margins_costs.quote: During the year under review, loss of CPP has been declined due to better realization and reduction in overheads.

margins_costs.claim: Cost optimization measures across sourcing, standardization, and process efficiency yielded significant savings.
margins_costs.quote: Various cost optimisation driven by way of alternate sourcing, standardization, process improvements and operational efficiency improvements has led significant savings.

margins_costs.claim: Excessive production capacity added to the market led to a persistent fall in selling prices and losses in the CPP segment.
margins_costs.quote: Loss of CPP segment is incurred during the year caused by persistent fall in selling prices on account of excessive production capacity added in the market.

margins_costs.claim: Higher production costs relative to the previous year caused declines in operating profit margin, net profit margin, and return on net worth.
margins_costs.quote: *Operating Profit Margin, Net Profit Margin and Return on Net Worth are declined as cost of production was relatively high as compared to previous year.

margins_costs.claim: Energy conservation measures via turbine replacement are expected to save approximately 1.00 Ton/hour of steam worth Rs. 100.00 Lakh per year.
margins_costs.quote: Saving of approx. 1.00 Ton/hour steam i.e. saving per year = Rs. 100.00 Lakh

margins_costs.claim: Net profit declined due to negative returns in the CPP segment caused by falling selling prices.
margins_costs.quote: Net profit during the year declined due to negative return on CPP Segment caused by persistent fall in selling prices on account of excessive production capacity added in the market.

margins_costs.claim: The company faced challenges from volatile crude prices, rising raw material costs, dumping of acrylic fibre, and foreign exchange fluctuations.
margins_costs.quote: Despite various challenges such as volatility in crude prices and abnormal rise in raw material prices, dumping of acrylic fibre by Turkey, China, Thailand and Belarus, foreign exchange fluctuations, the Company is focused on improvement in its growth and in a position to achieve a better turnover as compared to previous year.

orders_capacity.claim: The company's installed capacity for acrylic products is 42,000 MT per annum.
orders_capacity.quote: The production capacity to produce Acrylic products of the Company is 42,000 MT PA.

orders_capacity.claim: In FY 2024-25, acrylic fiber production reached 35,198 MT and sales reached 33,850 MT.
orders_capacity.quote: During the year under review, the Company has recorded production of 35,198 MT and Sale of 33,850 MT, as against production of 31,534 MT and Sale of 31,685 MT respectively during the previous year.

orders_capacity.claim: The installed capacity for CPP film is 10,000 MT per annum.
orders_capacity.quote: The Company’s production capacity to produce CPP film is 10000 MT PA.

orders_capacity.claim: CPP film production stood at 6,343 MT and sales stood at 6,409 MT during FY 2024-25.
orders_capacity.quote: During the year under review, the production and sale of CPP film was 6,343 MT and 6,409 MT respectively as against production of 6,463 MT and sale of 6,476 MT respectively during the previous year.

orders_capacity.claim: In FY 2023-24, CPP film production reached 6,463 MT and sales reached 6,476 MT.
orders_capacity.quote: During the year under review, the production and sale of CPP film was 6,463 MT and 6,476 MT respectively as against production of 7,663 MT and sale of 7,640 MT respectively during the previous year.

orders_capacity.claim: The company produced 36,425 MT and sold 35,260 MT of Acrylic products during the year.
orders_capacity.quote: During the year under review, the Company has recorded production of 36,425 MT and Sale of 35,260 MT, as against production of 29,652 MT and Sale of 30,918 MT respectively during the previous year.

orders_capacity.claim: Production and sales of CPP film increased to 7,663 MT and 7,640 MT respectively during the year.
orders_capacity.quote: During the year under review, the production and sale of CPP film increased to 7,663 MT and 7,640 MT respectively as against production of 6,348 MT and sale of 6,210 MT respectively during the previous year.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board decided not to recommend any dividend for FY 2024-25.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year under review the Board of Directors decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year 2024-25.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board decided not to transfer any amount to the General Reserve for FY 2024-25.
capital_allocation.quote: The Board of Directors of your company, has decided not to transfer any amount to the General Reserve for the year ended 31st March, 2025.

capital_allocation.claim: No dividend was recommended for FY 2023-24 as internal accruals were deployed to set up the Ethanol Plant.
capital_allocation.quote: As the Company’s internal accruals is being utilized to set-up Ethanol Plant, the Board of Directors decided not to recommend any dividend for the financial year 2023-24.

capital_allocation.claim: The company did not accept or renew any public deposits during the year under review.
capital_allocation.quote: During the year under review, your Company has neither accepted nor renewed any deposits within the meaning of Section 73 of the Companies Act, 2013 and the Companies (Acceptance of Deposits) Rules, 2014.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board of Directors decided not to transfer any amount to reserves for FY 2023-24.
capital_allocation.quote: The Board of Directors of your company, has decided not to transfer any amount to the Reserves for the year under review.

capital_allocation.claim: The Board decided to retain earnings to strengthen financials and did not recommend a dividend.
capital_allocation.quote: The Board of Directors decided to plough back the earnings to strengthen the financials of the Company and not to recommend dividend for the year under review.

risks_headwinds.claim: Fluctuations in USD vs. INR impact the company's margins because it depends on imported raw materials.
risks_headwinds.quote: Additionally, since the Company is dependent upon imports, the fluctuation in foreign exchange i.e. USD vs. INR has also a bearing on the margin of the Company.

risks_headwinds.claim: Ethanol product prices are fixed by Oil Marketing Companies, leaving the company with no pricing control.
risks_headwinds.quote: The prices of ethanol products are determined by Oil Marketing Companies (“OMC”) and the Company has no control on the prices.

risks_headwinds.claim: The company faces key risks including geopolitical tensions, supply chain disruptions, subdued global economic conditions, and cyber security threats.
risks_headwinds.quote: Geo-political tensions including supply chain disruption, subdued global economic conditions, changes in government policies and trade sanctions and restrictions, intense competition from local and global players, regulatory changes and cyber security threats are key risks which expose the Company to potential challenges and uncertainties.

risks_headwinds.claim: Fluctuations in USD exchange rates and crude oil price increases driven by international conflicts pose risks to the company's margins.
risks_headwinds.quote: Further, since the Company is dependent upon imported raw materials, movement in USD and increase in crude oil prices due to ongoing Israel-Hamas war and Russia-Ukraine war may affect the margin.

risks_headwinds.claim: Dumping of acrylic fibre from China, Thailand, and Belarus created business headwinds during the year.
risks_headwinds.quote: Despite various challenges such as volatility in crude prices and raw material prices, dumping of acrylic fibre by China, Thailand and Belarus, foreign exchange fluctuations, the Company is focused on improvement in its revenue and net profit.

risks_headwinds.claim: Crude price volatility due to the Russia-Ukraine War impacted raw material prices.
risks_headwinds.quote: The fluctuation in crude affects the raw material prices to some extent and during the year under the review, the crude prices remained volatile and witnessed a continued rise due to Russia-Ukraine War.

risks_headwinds.claim: The CPP Film Market is highly competitive due to the presence of multiple vendors.
risks_headwinds.quote: The CPP Film Market is highly competitive owing to the presence of multiple vendors in the market.

risks_headwinds.claim: Stringent packaging regulations and environmental pressures may restrain growth.
risks_headwinds.quote: On the other hand, stringent regulations concerning packaging, changing consumer preferences and environmental pressures may restrain the growth to some extent.

risks_headwinds.claim: The global economy faces headwinds from high energy costs, logistics issues, and international trade costs.
risks_headwinds.quote: Global economy is likely to be hit by continuing high energy cost, logistics issues and costs in international trade.

risks_headwinds.claim: Tightening monetary policies by central banks to curb inflation may impact consumption.
risks_headwinds.quote: Tightening of monetary policies by Central banks to curb inflation may have necessary impact which will impact consumption in general including Acrylic Fiber & CPP Films Industry.

management_commitments.claim: The company is exploring options to grow exports and expects to improve export volume in future years.
management_commitments.quote: The Company has exported to Dubai, Peru, Thailand, Morrocco, Tunisia, Nepal, Ukraine, Turkey, Algeria, Kenya, Brazil, Poland, Lebanon etc. and is exploring possibilities of increasing exports and it is hopeful to achieve better exports in the coming years.

management_commitments.claim: The company expects to commence commercial production of its 150 KLPD grain-based ethanol project by September 2024.
management_commitments.quote: Further, the Company has already initiated steps to establish grain based Ethanol Project with a production capacity of 150 KLPD and it is expected to commence commercial production of Ethanol by September, 2024.

management_commitments.claim: Mr. Satya Prakash Gupta is re-appointed as Whole Time Director designated as Director - Operations for a three-year period from May 29, 2024 to May 28, 2027.
management_commitments.quote: The appointment as Whole Time Director designated as Director – Operations for a period of three consecutive years w.e.f 29th May, 2024 to 28th May, 2027

management_commitments.claim: The company plans to fund the remaining project cost of Rs. 59.58 crores for the Ethanol Plant from internal accruals.
management_commitments.quote: The remaining project cost of Rs. 59.58 will be met out of the Company’s internal accruals.

management_commitments.claim: The company is focusing on increasing exports to mitigate the impact of foreign exchange and crude price movements.
management_commitments.quote: The Company is giving thrust on increasing the exports so that effect can be mitigated.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
